saints.name: St. Elizabeth of Portugal
saints.title: Queen and Widow
saints.shortBlurb: A queen who bore the name of her great-aunt and gave her life to peacemaking and the poor…
biography: Born at Zaragoza in 1271, daughter of King Peter III of Aragon, Elizabeth was named for her great-aunt, Elizabeth of Hungary, and given in marriage to King Denis of Portugal, the wedding celebrated in 1288 when she was seventeen. Amid a difficult marriage she kept the Divine Office daily, fasted, and poured out alms, founding hospitals at Coimbra, Santarém, and Leiria and providing dowries for poor girls.

She earned the name of Peacemaker: she took part in the Treaty of Alcañices in 1297, and in 1323, mounted on a mule, rode onto the field of Alvalade between the armies of her husband and her rebel son Afonso to prevent a civil war. Legend adds that bread she was carrying to the poor turned to roses when the king challenged her.

Widowed in 1325, she became a Franciscan tertiary beside the Poor Clares she had founded at Coimbra. In 1336, though ailing, she hurried to Estremoz to make peace between Afonso IV and Alfonso XI of Castile; the effort cost her life, and she died there on 4 July, aged sixty-five. Urban VIII canonized her; she is invoked for peace and by the falsely accused, whose calumnies she bore.
saints.knownFor: Making peace between warring kings and princes.
